t.E151.agn: In 2010 EFSA set the ADI for brilliant black BN at 5 mg/kg body weight; long-term cancer studies were negative. High intake in children under 10 could exceed this limit.
t.E151.body: In rats, 94–98% of orally administered brilliant black BN was excreted in faeces within 40 hours and less than 5% in urine; only trace amounts remained in tissues.
t.E151.eff.0.t: The daily limit may be exceeded
t.E151.prod: An azo dye produced by chemical synthesis.
t.E151.pw.0: According to EFSA, the daily intake limit may be exceeded in children who consume high amounts of this dye.
t.E151.regx.0: ADI 5 mg/kg; may be exceeded in high-consuming children.
t.E151.summary: A synthetic, black-violet azo dye. It is used in black confectionery and fish roe substitutes.
